kurz: Water is the main ingredient in almost every food. It caps the temperature at 100 °C, dissolves substances and makes starch [[quellen|swell]].
bild_im_kopf: The quiet lead actor: where there is water, it gets no hotter than 100 °C.
was_passiert: As long as water is present, the temperature stays at boiling point. Only once it is gone can things brown. It dissolves salt, sugar and aromas and allows starch and [[glutenbildung|gluten]] to form.
faustregeln: For a crust: get rid of the water. For tenderness: keep it.
At altitude water boils below 100 °C, and cooking times get longer.

rolle.rolle: forms the gluten network with flour
